title: Hidden relays with positive capacitance match direct transfer within 5% on 0-100 Hz in 31 passive models from Allen data
abstract: We tested whether finite-band electrical transfer separates a direct junction from a passive hidden relay. We extended a published DC construction with positive node capacitances and derived a sufficient error bound. With no positive lower bound on hidden capacitance and with unknown membrane leaks, a circuit with no direct edge can approach a direct-edge response over any fixed finite frequency band. The ideal high-frequency limits still differ. We applied the method to 31 reciprocal reference models from Allen mouse visual cortex slice data. A hidden capacitance below a pair-specific bound of 0.061-0.525 pF kept complex cross-transfer error within 5% over 0-100 Hz, for any fixed positive recorded-node capacitances. In the tested relay construction with 100 pF at each recorded node, 1 pF hidden capacitance exceeded 5% error in all 31 references on the sampled band. Separate full circuit calculations, a denser grid, and 1,000 random circuits passed numerical checks. The responses are model examples, not measured transients or evidence for hidden neurons. Reciprocal adjustment, separate resistance measurements, unknown leaks, small required capacitances, and passive lumped nodes limit biological inference. The package supplies a proof, code, derived evidence, source hashes, and reproduction instructions.
